page0.text: It is an altar enshrining the stars.

page1.text:
Fire blazes as if to connect heaven and earth.
Flickering flames illuminate the dark cave,
searing the canopy above.
But this is no godly shrine.
The "sky" it connects to is deep underground,
and the burning torch is black, not red.
The air is murky, the wind is stagnant, and the water oozing down the walls is the color of poison.

page2.text:
This underground kingdom is said to have been the lair of a dragon. In fact, it is modeled after the stomach of a dragon.
None who visit this place are human.
Those who seek salvation in this otherwordly realm, who rejoice in this bizarre sight, must only be the sort of demons who flee the light of the sun.

page3.text:
"GUH..."
A skull-masked face chokes in the midst of the realm.
Lit by dark crimson, he is the Servant Assassin, who lost his Master to Kirei Kotomine.

page4.text:
"I suppose this is as far as I go. My body can no longer last without magical energy."
The white skull creeps along a wall.
Ahead of him stands a girl.
Dressed in black curses, she stares absently at the approaching skull

page5.text:
"Tsss... Finally here.
Lord Mage. I do not see you, but are you alive?"
He stops five or six meters from the girl.
Stuck to a wall like a spider, Assassin calls out into the void.

page6.text:
"...Yes. Well met, Assassin."
Finally, someone answers.
The old mage's voice rings out in the void.
The old man should have been eliminated by Kirei, but here he is, alive and well.

page7.text:
It is only logical.
The Zouken Matou which was crushed in the forest was no more than a swarm of worms.
His real body which anchors his soul to the world sleeps elsewhere, in a safe location.
Even the priest's holy words cannot destroy the old mage, as long as the insects that comprise his real body remain intact.

page8.text:
"It does pain me to lose my limbs and all. I can't even send you magical energy right now. And it would be difficult to gather a new body on the surface.
...Hm. This will be an ordeal, but perhaps it's time. Sakura, make a contract with Assassin. We need a new bodyguard now after you lost Berserker."
The old mage intones an order.
The black cursed girl, Sakura Matou, doesn't respond.
She ignores the absolute authority of the old man and continues staring out into space with lightless eyes.

page9.text:
"...What are you doing, Sakura? Are you going to disobey me?"
A threatening current runs beneath his irritated tone.
The old man is slightly on edge.
He is angry at the girl's ineptitude for losing Berserker and letting Illyasviel slip away.

page10.text:
"...Sakura. I will say it one more time. Are you going to disobey me?"
Cold contempt.
The girl has never defied the old man when he speaks like that.
Not out of fear, but because his dominance is absolute.
She does fear him, of course.
But she is literally unable to defy him.
Reason being, her heart is...

page11.text:
"Wait, Lord Mage. I think her mind is broken. She had to take in so much. A feeble girl could not be expected to survive."
"...Hm?"
The old man's irritation vanishes.
...He returns to calm silence.
In this dark crimson pit, there is a sound of a slithering worm.

page12.text:
"Hmm. It appears so. I thought she'd hold out a while longer. How anticlimactic."
The old mage sounds both disappointed and utterly enthused.
The girl doesn't answer.
Her mind has been swallowed by the darkness.

page13.text:
"Then will you take her, as planned?"
"You make it sound so terrible. I did not plan for this. It is the only option left. Sakura Matou's mind is gone. She won't be able to control that monster now.
I know it is cruel, but I have no choice but to eat my empty granddaughter."
He snickers.
The laughter comes from the girl's throat.
The old mage is laughing using the empty Sakura's vocal cords.

page14.text:
"Then you should hurry. Without magical energy, my body is about to fade away."
"Hm, yes. Let's begin, then.
It's really too bad, Sakura. I wanted to let you have the glory of acquiring the Holy Grail after you did such a good job raising that thing. Oh, well.
If you must blame anyone, blame yourself for delaying the ritual when you let Illyasviel escape.

page15.text:
A crunching sound.
A worm wriggles its way into the girl's neck.
It can't be seen.
There is no worm crawling under her skin.
Not from the outside.
There was never any escape for the girl, not from the twisted thoughts nestled against her heart.

page16.text:
Zouken Matou, insect-user.
His real body, the host for his decaying soul, is the pseudo-nerves enervating Sakura Matou's heart.

page17.text:
"Kuh. Your body hasn't fully changed, but I won't complain. I will simply take command in place of its absent owner.
Goodbye, Sakura. You were quite durable for a test subject. You entertained me quite well...!"
There is a slippery sound of wriggling blood vessels.
Zouken Matou's rotten spiritual body orders his worm body to eat the girl's brain.

page19.text: "There's no need for that, Grandfather. I'm perfectly fine."

page20.text: The girl places a hand on her chest and opens her eyes.

page21.text:
"Oh? I thought it swallowed you, but you're still hanging on... Very well. Sakura, the situation has changed somewhat. I can no longer maintain Assassin.
It will put a burden on you, but make a new contract with Assassin in my place."
The old mage issues a command as he always does.
However, the girl shakes her head in denial.

page22.text:
"...What is the meaning of this, Sakura?"
"I told you, Grandfather. That won't be necessary."
Her icy voice rings in the gloom.
Suddenly,
the white skull on the wall is swallowed by something dark and enormous.

page23.text:
"Geeeh!?"
"What!?"
Their astonishment comes too late.
Assassin's entire body is compressed in a single attack, leaving only his mask intact.
"GAH... AHH, AHHHHHHHH!?"
The mask falls.
Beneath the white mask, where his face should be,
is only another skull.

page24.text:
"Hehe. That's it? I was wondering what his face would look like, but he never had a face at all.
What a boring person. You weren't hiding your face. You just wanted everyone to think that you had one."
"Geeh...DAMN YOU, girl..."
"You lost your face, threw away your name, and you still want eternity. But too bad. If you want eternity, you should wish to live forever like Grandfather.
Even the Holy Grail can't go back in time and give you back a name that you lost."

page25.text:
"Disappear, lord of the mountain. You're nobody, just an assassin. You will never be a true Hassan."
"GEEEH, GYAAAAAAAAAARRRRGH!!!"
The shadows swallow his death cry.
The skull-masked Assassin is devoured without a trace.

page26.text:
"Guh... Have you lost your mind!? What are you doing, you fool!?"
The old man's confusion borders on madness.
Is he shocked by the sudden development, or being driven mad by indescribable terror?

page27.text:
The girl laughs at the old man who used to control her.
"He attacked Senpai twice, you know.
That's why I killed him. After all, I'm the only one allowed to hurt Senpai."
"Wha..."
"And Grandfather, you don't need him to protect you anymore. I felt bad for him, so I wanted to give him a vacation."

page28.text:
Then, there is a wet sound.
The girl plunges her fingers into her own body, tearing out the worm burrowed deep inside, in an act of psychic surgery.

page29.text:
"Nnngh!!!"
What to call this terror, this confusion?
The girl gouges out her own body, tearing her own nerves to shreds, all while giggling coolly.

page30.text:
"Wha... What are you doing, Sakura!?"
He wriggles.
With lightless eyes, the girl examines the thing that is her grandfather, the thing calling itself her grandfather, the thing that seems to have been her grandfather.

page31.text:
"Oh. That was easy. I always thought you'd be bigger, Grandfather."
In fact, the worm serving as Zouken Matou's main body was not always this diminutive.
The old mage changed his host to a more suitable worm in order to parasitize the girl's heart.
To do that it needed to be smaller than a heart.
In retrospect, his eccentric taste turned out to be his downfall.

page32.text:
"Sakura...Sakura, how dare..."
"I should thank that priest. If he hadn't erased the rest of you, you might have really eaten me."

page33.text:
She's seen right through him.
No, this was inevitable from the beginning.
The old mage never bothered to hide his objective, and the girl could not defy his will.
So there was no problem.
He only ever treated her as his eventual replacement body.
So... she only had to wait until it was time to raise the flag of rebellion.

page34.text:
"W-wait. Wait, wait, wait!
It's not what you think, Sakura! Taking over your body was the last resort. As long as your mind was intact, I was going to let you have the gate. I just want the Matous to have the glory.
You win, and you can have everything now, Sakura...!"

page35.text:
The worm wriggles.
She gently smiles at the filthy creature between her fingers.

page36.text: "That's all the more reason to do this. I don't need you anymore, Grandfather. Now I can open the gate on my own."

page37.text:
Something inconceivable is happening.
The old mage made only one mistake.

page38.text:
"...! Wait! I said wait, Sakura...!
I was doing this for your sake, you know!
How, how could you betray your debt to—"

page39.text:
"Goodbye, Grandfather.
You must be tired after spending two hundred years underground.
Now you can disappear."
The old man raised the girl too well.
He failed to notice the darkness within her and mistook it for purity.

page40.text:
...Only the girl remains at the altar.
The flickering black blaze delights in the girl's independence, a personification of itself.
